title: New Day
essence: The poet dismounts at a ruined chapel on a foggy shore and, as the morning comes, a new temple builds itself with him: white, clean, modern, counted into being piece by piece. He walks laps round its edgeless pool, reads from a journal, walks on the still sea, and in the last movement the sun clears the ridge and a line of light runs across the valley to the finished temple and to him.
palette_notes: Blue hour and slate from the night shore still (ef9f6c7e); fog grey from 993cc7a2; dark tree-green hills and soft sea blue-green from the pool stills (08fe12af, 58cbb4ca). The temple is chalk white, never pure white, warmed by dawn rose and sun gold. Rust (#a94022, the district colour) is kept for the chapel stone and rubble, the old that the new replaces. The world's single accent is the finial's tip, reached only when the building is complete.

full_text.line: Even here is chilly in the morning.
River rafting fall covers the seas in the distance
and hugs the bases of tree-covered hills.
This world is at peace.
In silent resounds, choir chords calm the nerves of things I can't control
and offer them as keepsakes back to the higher powers.
Exhausted emotions carry forward a diminishing flame
to emit jazz tuned lyrics that heat and dry the morning dew.
All the remnants of the destruction revealed in the sunlight.
We can rebuild this temple.
It's a new day.
The catharsis evoked by loss in the painful crawl
along the cobblestone boulevards of broken dreams.
I can close a chapter and open a journal stored away
from moments of great clarity.
Words written from life's triumphs to offer a blueprint
of keeping faith alive and as majestic.
When words are read aloud and sung alone as gospels
to the lonely mirror's midnight hours,
the left tears drying with time that is common to past.
We can embrace a new day.
We can receive a new day.
We can welcome a new day.
Everything I've known and learned,
every circumference of life we're celebrating and believing
is here together in this sacred place,
reveling in the sunlight of a new beginning
with this world and a heart at peace.

insights: There is only ever one drawing of the temple: the same 19 cards on the same ground line in every movement, just more of them.
Every change of light goes one way and is a hard swap (fog edge, dawn bands, ray wedges, terminator), never a dimmer.
Pieces arrive and then do not move; the stillness between arrivals is what makes them feel built.
The pool is the one place a mirror is honest: shoot the top half and flip it, no visible edge.
Walking on water is a calm patch that travels with him, not ripples reacting to him.
Keep the poet darker than the white stone and clear of the platform footprint, or the building swallows him.

Atlas: the Halfworld/markov frames (foundry/11-03, 11-04, sets/5380dc5ec9f0f55c-5) already build the temple as a black six-column silhouette counted up out of a dotted ground; our white 19 cards should read identically in silhouette at blue hour.
Atlas: the temple has no lamps; its light is white ceramic lit by the sky and doubled in the pools. Paint the pools as mirror cards and let the sky carry every change.
Atlas: 11 and 12 share one frame (the mirror hall / portico pool). Lock that plate's layout now so 12 is the same cards, filled.
future: The completed white temple can stand in 14 as the sacred place everyone gathers in.
The hill ridge and sea carry into 13's harbour light and 14.
The journal returns whenever the poet reads aloud.
The 19-piece assembly technique is the template for any later self-building architecture.

atlas.district_language: From Cenotaph Rail to the White Temple: the Shore is where time-lapse is the native tense, so every change is a card arriving or a band swapping, never a camera move through space. Cenotaph Rail gives the arrival: wet stone shore steps under the mountain, Wardens' lanterns still burning at dawn, a cold grey sea; it has no light of its own. The White Temple has no lamps either: its light is the white ceramic lit by the sky, and its pools hold the sky exactly. Paint the temple chalk white with one cyan seam (the Glaziers' line, the brightest seam in the city) and keep the chapel's dark stone walls visible under the flood line inside it. Pools are mirror cards: the temple painted inverted, sky first. Hills are one dark ridge silhouette reused in every movement; fog is a flat grey band card. Never show: ornament, gold, crowds (12 has the hall full), a sun drawn below the ridge.

staging.name: Arrival on the chilly shore
staging.shot: extreme wide from the water, locked off: sea strip foreground, the shore steps with lantern dots at left, the chapel ruin small centre, ridge silhouette behind; a fog band card slides in across the sea; the bike card enters down the shore road and stops; slow push only by scaling the plate.

staging.name: Remnants in the sunlight
staging.shot: low and close on the rubble floor card: fallen stones, a broken tambourine rim with two jingles; a hard-edged light wedge card slides across them left to right and the dew sheen layer drops out where it passes.

staging.name: The temple builds itself
staging.shot: locked-off frontal wide on the chapel footprint: POET raises his palms and a white course arrives under them (3-step replacement), then columns, then beams; each card stays. Intercut a side-on medium of him on the stylobate with columns sliding in between him and the lens.

staging.name: Choir chords in the new nave (inferred)
staging.shot: symmetrical wide down the colonnade: white column cards in two rows receding, sunbeam wedges between them, POET appearing and disappearing behind each column as he walks; the chapel's dark stone kept below the line on the back wall.

staging.name: Journal and the lonely mirror (inferred)
staging.shot: POET seated at the pool lip, profile, the journal open on his knee; the pool card below holds his inverted figure exactly; cut to over-shoulder onto the page, then down the mirror hall of white piers on black water with him small at the edge.

staging.name: Welcoming the new day
staging.shot: reverse from inside: dark interior frame card, the doorway a bright card of sea and sky, POET's silhouette in it raising both arms; then exterior hero wide: the sun card clears the ridge, the terminator band sweeps the valley floor card left to right onto the finished white temple and him.

heroes.name: The Shore Steps
heroes.in_poem: the bike comes down to the shore at the foot of the steps (11.0); the lanterns on the landings are still burning from the Wardens' dusk lighting.
heroes.build_as_cards: a stair as a stack of 6-8 stepped strips with a landing every storey, wet-sheen layer on each tread; lantern cards with a small coded flame on each landing; the old station wall as a tall dark card at left; water card at the bottom edge. Lanterns go out one by one as the sun clears the ridge.

heroes.name: The Temple's Pools
heroes.in_poem: the infinity pool he walks round and reads at (11.4) and the still water that doubles the finished temple in the welcome (11.5); laid where the chapel's floor was.
heroes.build_as_cards: each pool is a glossy mirror card with the temple, columns and sky painted inverted and slightly darker; an edge-less lip (no rim card on the sea side) so the pool meets the sea line; ripple is a coded displacement only when he steps; the tambourine shards set into the lip as tiny bright plates.

heroes.name: The clock tower
heroes.in_poem: the atlas lists it for New Day (climb the stair to the room behind the clock faces); the breakdown does not stage it. Optional: the alcove of 11.4 as the room behind a clock face, the journal read in the light coming through the dial, its gears still. Low priority.
heroes.build_as_cards: exterior: a red-brick shaft card with stone trim and verdigris roof, one dial card; interior: the back of the dial as a translucent disc with reversed numerals, a gear train as 3-4 overlapping cog cards on pins (static, or turning one tooth per line), a stair strip climbing the shaft.
